get.description: Returns the organizations the authenticated user belongs to. Call this right after Firebase sign-in to decide whether to show an organization picker (`needsSelection: true`) or proceed straight into the app.

put.description: Marks one of the user's organizations as the default. Subsequent requests are scoped to this organization automatically.

post.description:
Generates a new API key for the **calling staff member** and returns the raw key **once**. There is no `{id}` in the path — the staff record is derived from the Firebase token. Admins cannot generate keys for other staff; every staff member manages only their own credential.

Only the SHA-256 hash and the 8-char prefix are persisted — the raw value cannot be recovered after this response, so the UI must show it to the user immediately and prompt them to store it securely.

Calling this endpoint when a key already exists **rotates** it: the previous key is invalidated atomically and only the new one will authenticate going forward.

The resulting key inherits the staff user's organization scope and permissions. Use it via the `X-Api-Key` header on any subsequent request — see the [API keys guide](/guides/api-keys) for the full flow.

200.description: API key generated. The `apiKey` field is the only place the raw key is returned.

400.description: The caller is not a `STAFF` user (clients cannot have API keys).

403.description: The caller authenticated via `X-Api-Key`. Generating, rotating or revoking an API key requires a Firebase Bearer token to prevent privilege escalation from a leaked key.

get.description:
Returns the masked prefix and creation timestamp of the calling staff member's current API key. The raw key is never included — this endpoint exists so a UI can show *"key created on 2026-05-21 starting with `dst_a3b4…`"* without exposing the full credential. Returns `null` when no key has been generated.

Unlike `POST` and `DELETE`, this read-only endpoint works under both `bearerAuth` and `apiKeyAuth` — the caller may inspect their own key under either authentication mode.

200.description: Current API key info, or `null` when no key exists

delete.description: Clears the calling staff member's API key. After this call, any request that uses the previous key will be rejected with `401`. Use this when a key may have been leaked. Generating a new key with `POST` after revocation is fine — it will start fresh.

403.description: The caller authenticated via `X-Api-Key`. Revoking an API key requires a Firebase Bearer token.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of products. For full-text search by name/SKU/UPC, prefer `GET /api/search/v1/products`.
Returns the images and other media attached to a product, ordered by `order`.

post.description: Returns media for many products at once, keyed by product id. Use this on the catalog grid instead of N+1 requests.

get.description: Returns every UOM configured for the product (e.g. case of 12, six-pack of 6, single unit) with the conversion factor and `isDefault` flag.

post.description: Returns per-product UOM price lists for the given products, honouring the price list assigned to `clientId`. Use this on the catalog and the cart whenever the active client changes.
Returns available stock for many products at once, optionally scoped to a warehouse. Use this on the catalog grid.

get.description: Returns the per-warehouse stock breakdown, plus lots, serials and the recent inventory transactions for a single product.
Returns the lots tracked for a product. The mobile app uses this to surface the nearest-expiring lot on the Product Detail screen.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text on name, RFC and email

get.description: Returns a paginated list of orders. For full-text search across client, folio and invoice number, prefer `GET /api/search/v1/orders`.

parameters.name: deliveryStatusIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of delivery status UUIDs

post.description: Creates an order. Set `status: "DRAFT"` to save the cart without confirming, or `"CONFIRMED"` to commit and (optionally) trigger invoice generation with `markAsInvoiced: true`.

put.description: Full replacement of a DRAFT order. For confirmed orders use PATCH semantics on `/status`, `/delivery-status` etc.

patch.description: Advances the order through its delivery timeline (e.g. PENDING → IN_PROGRESS → DELIVERED).
Triggers CFDI generation and stamps the order with an `invoiceNumber`. Idempotent.
Voids an invoiced order. Returns the updated order with `status: "VOIDED"`.

get.description: Returns the CFDI 4.0 invoice PDF. Only valid for orders that have been invoiced.

Returns the full event log for an order — creation, delivery transitions and payment activity — ordered ascending by `occurredAt`. Powers the **SEGUIMIENTO** UI in jadix, storefront and mobile.

Events have a `type` of `GENERAL` (order lifecycle), `DELIVERY` (logistics transitions; `status` carries the new delivery status UUID — resolve via [`/delivery-statuses`](/api-reference/orders/delivery-statuses)) or `PAYMENT` (payment added/removed; `status` is the resulting order payment state and `notes` is `"<amount> <paymentMethodId>"`).

post.description: Records a payment for a client. Use `allocations` to split it across one or more orders.

get.description: Returns the per-organization charge configuration (shipping, IVA, card commissions, etc.) shown in the Cart's CARGOS section.
Returns the ordered list of delivery statuses configured for the organization (e.g. Confirmada, Preparada, En tránsito, Entregada). Drives the timeline scaffold on the order detail screen.
Returns the recent sale prices of a product to a specific client. Drives the "Última venta" hint in the cart.
Full-text search across product name, SKU and UPC, with category, brand, stock, price-range filters and sort. Backs the catalog grid on the mobile app and the products list in Jadix.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text search across name, SKU and UPC

parameters.name: warehouseId
parameters.description: Scope results to products that have an inventory entry in this warehouse. When set, each product's `inventory` array in the response is reduced to **only** the entry for this warehouse — callers operating in a single-warehouse flow (e.g. mobile POS) get a self-consistent view where summing `availableQty` reflects only the chosen warehouse. Without this param, `inventory` returns every warehouse the product exists in.

parameters.name: hasStock
parameters.description: "true" or "false" — filter by in-stock availability (`inventory[].availableQty > 0`). Combine with `warehouseId` to scope the stock check to a single warehouse.

parameters.name: priceMin
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `price`. Negative values are ignored.

parameters.name: priceMax
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `price`. Negative values are ignored.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Result ordering. `relevance` sorts by `catalogPriority` ascending (products without priority go last), tie-broken by `createdAt` descending. Defaults to `created_desc` on this endpoint.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: Restrict results to the variants of one product group (DIS-889).

get.description: Full-text search across client name, order folio and invoice number, with the same filter surface as `GET /api/orders/v1`.
Aggregates the same filter set as `GET /api/search/v1/orders` into counts by delivery status and payment status. Drives the badges on the Orders list tabs.

parameters.name: thisWeekFrom
parameters.description: ISO date for the start of the "this week" window

post.description: Returns the total qty incoming for the given products from open purchase orders. Does not break down by PO; see the gap noted in the Product Detail guide.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of quotations scoped to the caller. Sales reps only see quotations they created; managers see every quotation in the org. For full-text search across client and quote number, prefer `GET /api/search/v1/quotations`.

post.description: Creates a quotation in `DRAFT` status. Unlike orders, creating a quotation does **NOT** validate or commit inventory — quotations are a sales proposal, stock is only touched when the quotation is converted to an order.

put.description: Full replacement of a `DRAFT` quotation. Once a quotation is in `CONFIRMED` status (i.e. it has been converted to an order) it is read-only — this endpoint will return `409 Conflict`.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the quotation. Only `DRAFT` quotations can be deleted; converted quotations are kept for audit alongside their order.

patch.description: Transitions a quotation between `DRAFT` and `CONFIRMED`. Note that `CONFIRMED` is also set automatically by `POST /{id}/convert` and once set the quotation becomes read-only — use this endpoint mainly to flip a manually-confirmed quotation back to draft.

post.description:
Creates an `Order` from the quotation, marks the quotation as `CONFIRMED`, and links them via the order's `quoteId` and the quotation's `orderId`.

**Preconditions** (return `409 Conflict` on failure):
- Quotation status must be `DRAFT` and not already converted (`orderId == null`).
- `clientId` must be set — anonymous quotations cannot be converted.
- Every line must have a `warehouseId` — quotations allow lines without a warehouse, but orders do not.

**Side effects** — unlike `POST /api/orders/v1`, conversion runs the full order-create flow on the line items, which means:
- Inventory is validated (the order is rejected if any line has insufficient stock) and shipped against the chosen warehouse.
- The order is created in `CONFIRMED` status, not `DRAFT`.
- Order timeline + Kafka order-created events fire as if the order had been created directly.

If the order creation fails (stock, validation, etc.) the quotation stays in `DRAFT` and no inventory is touched.

get.summary: Last quoted price for client × product
get.description: Returns the most recent unit price quoted to this client for this product — used by the POS / order form to pre-fill the price when re-quoting a known client.

post.description: Returns the total qty currently committed to open quotations for the given products.

put.description: The body accepts `variantsEnabled` to opt the organization into the product variants (groups) model. It is false by default; while it is false the group endpoints answer 403 and products behave exactly as before. The product service caches the flag for 60 seconds. See [Product variants](/guides/product-variants).

post.summary: List public media by product ids
Get public price lists by products

get.description: For organizations with variants enabled the template carries two extra columns, `Variant Group` and `Variant Attributes` (`Color=Mustard; Size=L`), and the export fills them — so export → edit in Excel → re-import preserves the grouping. See [Product variants](/guides/product-variants).

post.description: Rows may carry the `Variant Group` and `Variant Attributes` columns to place the product in a variant group; the upsert is idempotent, so re-importing the same file does not duplicate anything. See [Product variants](/guides/product-variants).

Rows may carry the `Variant Group` and `Variant Attributes` columns to place the product in a variant group; the upsert is idempotent, so re-importing the same file does not duplicate anything. See [Product variants](/guides/product-variants).

**Variant columns (organizations with variants enabled).** Each item also accepts `variant_group` (the group name, created when it does not exist) and `variant_attributes` in the form `Color=Mustard; Size=L`, where the order of the pairs defines the axis order. The upsert is idempotent — re-sending the same rows does not duplicate groups, axes, values or memberships. A malformed `variant_attributes` value is reported as a row warning and the product is still created, just not grouped. See [Product variants](/guides/product-variants).

post.summary: Get price lists by I ds

get.summary: Count clients by price list I ds

post.description:
Creates a group and, optionally, its variation axes and their values in one call. The axes are ordered: the first one is the primary axis. Creating a group does not create any product — use Generate variants for that.

Requires the `products.create` permission.

get.description:
Paginated list of groups with their variant counts. Variants themselves are omitted — fetch a single group to get them.

Requires the `products.list` permission.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive search on the group name.

get.description:
Returns the group with its axes (ordered by position, values ordered too) and its variants.

Requires the `products.list` permission.

parameters.name: includeStock
parameters.description: When `true`, each variant carries `onHandQty` summed across warehouses.

put.description:
Updates the group's own fields. Set `propagatePricing: true` to also write the group's price and cost onto every member product — pricing lives on the product, so this is the only way a group edit reaches the variants.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the group and removes the membership rows. **The variant products are never deleted** — they stay in the catalog as ordinary products, keeping their SKU, UPCs, stock and history.

Requires the `products.delete` permission.

post.description:
Adds an axis (and optionally its values) to an existing group. Adding an axis to a group that already has variants leaves those variants without a value on the new axis until each one is updated.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

put.description:
Renames or reorders an axis. Axis names are unique per group, case-insensitively.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

delete.description:
Removes an axis and its values. Answers 409 when any variant still uses one of those values.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

post.description:
Adds a possible value to an axis, e.g. another colour. Values are unique per axis, case-insensitively.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

delete.description:
Removes a value from an axis. Answers 409 when a variant is using it.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

post.description:
Creates one product per requested combination, inheriting the group's price, cost, brand and active flag. Send an empty body to generate every missing combination.

With `?preview=true` nothing is written: the response lists the combinations with a suggested SKU and name and flags the ones that already exist, so a client can let the user edit them before committing.

The whole batch runs in a single transaction — one rejected combination creates no products at all.

Requires the `products.create` permission.

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: Set to `true` for a dry run that returns the suggested combinations without creating anything.

post.description:
Links a product that already exists to the group. Useful for catalogues that were built flat before variants were enabled. The product keeps its own price — attaching never rewrites it. Answers 409 when the product already belongs to a group or when the combination is taken.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

put.description:
Moves a variant to a different combination. Answers 409 when the target combination already exists.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

delete.description:
Unlinks a variant from its group. **The product survives** as an ordinary product with its stock and history; only the membership disappears.

Requires the `products.edit` permission.

bearerAuth.description: Firebase ID token issued after sign-in. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>`. The token alone determines both the authenticated user and the organization the request is scoped to.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description:
Long-lived API key bound to a `STAFF` user, prefixed `dst_`. Send as `X-Api-Key: dst_<32 chars>`. When present, takes precedence over the `Authorization` header — the key alone determines both the authenticated user and the organization scope (no need to set a default org or send a Firebase token).

**Key management endpoints (`POST` / `DELETE` on `/staff/me/api-key`) require Firebase Bearer auth and reject `X-Api-Key` with `403`.** This prevents a leaked key from minting or rotating itself. The read-only `GET /staff/me/api-key` works under both auth modes.

Generate a key via `POST /api/organizations/v1/staff/me/api-key`; see the [API keys guide](/guides/api-keys).

ValidationError.description: Validation failed. Message is localized via `Accept-Language`.

VariantsDisabled.description: Product variants are not enabled for this organization. Turn on Product Variants in Settings (organizations.variantsEnabled) first.

apiKey.description: The raw API key. Format: `dst_` + 32 alphanumeric chars. Returned **only** at generation time — store it immediately, it cannot be recovered.

prefix.description: First 8 chars of the raw key, safe to display for identification (`dst_` + 8 chars).
Masked prefix of the current key. The raw key is never returned by this endpoint.

variantsEnabled.description: Opts the organization into the product variants (groups) model. False by default; while it is false the group endpoints answer 403 and products behave exactly as before.

pieces.description: Pieces per UOM (e.g. 12 for a case of 12)

priceMin.description: Lowest `price` across the result set after every filter except `priceMin`/`priceMax` (same drill-down logic as the category and brand facet counts). Use to initialize the lower bound of a price-range slider. Zero when the result set is empty.

priceMax.description: Highest `price` across the result set after every filter except `priceMin`/`priceMax`. Use to initialize the upper bound of a price-range slider. Zero when the result set is empty.

allOf.description: Counts in `facets.categories` are computed with every active filter EXCEPT the category selection; same drill-down logic applies to `facets.brands`. Buckets with `count = 0` are excluded.

effectivePrice.description: Final price used at checkout: overridePrice if set, otherwise calculatedPrice.

defaultActive.description: Whether the charge is pre-checked in the cart by default.

shippingAddressFormatted.description: Single-line rendering of the shipping address. Auto-resolved by the order service from `shippingAddressId` at create/update time. Read-only.

billingAddressFormatted.description: Single-line rendering of the billing address. Auto-resolved by the order service from `billingAddressId` at create/update time. Read-only.

warehouseId.description: Optional on quotations; **required** when converting to an order.

clientId.description: Null for anonymous quotations created from the catalog before a client is known. Must be set before the quotation can be converted to an order.

status.description: `CONFIRMED` is set automatically once the quotation has been converted to an order; once set, the quotation becomes read-only.

source.description: Channel that originated the quotation: `web`, `pos`, `app` or `catalog`.

clientId.description: Optional at quotation creation — quotations may start anonymous and get a client assigned later. Required before `POST /{id}/convert`.

status.description: For `GENERAL` events: the new order status (e.g. `CREATED`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`). For `DELIVERY` events: the UUID of the new delivery status (resolve against [`/delivery-statuses`](/api-reference/orders/delivery-statuses)). For `PAYMENT` events: `UNPAID` | `PARTIAL` | `PAID` | `PAYMENT_REMOVED` | `REFUNDED`.

byUserId.description: Populated from the gateway-injected `x-user-id` header when the actor is a user (e.g. a storefront customer).

byStaffId.description: Populated from the gateway-injected `x-staff-id` header when the actor is a staff member.

notes.description: Free-form payload. For `PAYMENT` events when a payment is added: `"<amount> <paymentMethodId>"`. Empty otherwise.

markAsInvoiced.description: When true, the invoice service generates the CFDI synchronously after creating the order.

byDeliveryStatus.description: Counts keyed by delivery status id.

ProductVariantAttribute.description: One attribute name/value pair of a variant.

ProductGroupBlock.description: Variant-group block carried by a product. Present only when the product belongs to a group, so it is absent for every product of an organization that has not enabled variants.

variantLabel.description: Attribute values joined by a space; this is the field free-text search matches.

ProductGroupAttribute.description: A variation axis of the group. Position 0 is the primary axis.

ProductGroupVariant.description: One variant of the group. Every variant is a full product, so `productId` works anywhere a product id is accepted (orders, quotations, inventory, price lists).

upcs.description: UPCs are per variant and MAY repeat across variants of the same group.

onHandQty.description: Stock summed across warehouses. Only returned when the request passes includeStock=true.

ProductGroup.description: A group bundles products that share a style and pricing and differ only along the attribute axes. Price and cost live on the group and are copied to the member products; each variant keeps its own SKU, UPCs, images and stock.

skuPrefix.description: Base for suggested variant SKUs: prefix 5121 suggests 5121-MUS-L.

variants.description: Returned by the detail endpoint; omitted from list responses.

position.description: Axis order. Defaults to the position in the array.

UpdateProductGroupRequest.description: Every field is optional; omitted fields keep their current value.

propagatePricing.description: When true the group price and cost are written to every member product in one transaction. Leave it false to edit the group without touching the products.

position.description: Axis order. Defaults to the position in the array.

VariantCombinationRequest.description: One variant to create. attributeValueIds must contain exactly one value per axis of the group.

sku.description: Defaults to the suggested SKU when omitted.

name.description: Defaults to the suggested name when omitted.

GenerateVariantsRequest.description: Leave combinations empty to generate every combination that does not exist yet.

exists.description: True when a variant for this combination already exists.

totalCombinations.description: Size of the full cartesian product.

truncated.description: True when the response was capped at 500 combinations; generate them and request the preview again to continue.

productId.description: An existing product that does not belong to any group.
